slides.title: 9 symptoms nobody warns you about
slides.body: Every one of them is on the NHS list.

slides.title: Your heart racing
slides.body: A faster, slower or more noticeable heartbeat. The NHS says to mention palpitations to your GP.

slides.title: Aching joints
slides.body: Muscle aches and joint pains. For some women they carry on after menopause.

slides.title: Itchy skin
slides.body: Skin changes, including skin that feels dry and itchy.

slides.title: Weight around the middle
slides.body: Weight gain is common, and it often settles around the stomach and upper body.

slides.title: Worse headaches
slides.body: Headaches and migraines that are worse than they used to be.

slides.title: Brain fog
slides.body: Problems with memory and concentration. Words, names, why you walked into the room.

slides.title: Needing the loo more
slides.body: Needing to wee more often, or symptoms that feel like a UTI.

slides.title: Feeling anxious
slides.body: Low mood, mood swings, or feeling irritable and anxious. Poor sleep can make it worse.

slides.title: Sound familiar?
slides.body: These can have other causes too, so talk to your GP about anything new. Writing down when they happen makes that conversation easier.
